title: Layout Lab — CSS Grid, Flexbox & Container Query Playground
description: A layout playground where every box on the bench is placed by the exact stylesheet printed beneath it: switch between Grid and Flexbox, tune tracks, named areas, gaps, auto-fill versus auto-fit, wrapping, per-item flex-grow, spans and order. Drag the container narrower to watch a real container query stack the layout, load one of six recipes (holy grail, card grid, sidebar, masonry-ish, pancake stack, switcher), and copy the CSS.
prompt: Build 'Layout Lab', an interactive CSS Grid + Flexbox + container-query playground. Give me controls for grid-template-columns and areas, gap, auto-fill vs auto-fit with minmax, flex-wrap/grow/basis and alignment, and let me click a single box to give it its own span, grow, basis or order. The boxes must reflow live, and I want a draggable container edge so I can squeeze it and watch container queries switch the layout. Show the grid tracks as an overlay so the auto-fill/auto-fit difference is visible, not just described. Include six ready-made recipes — holy grail, card grid, sidebar, masonry-ish, pancake stack and a switcher — each with a one-line explanation of why it works. The CSS panel must be the real stylesheet that is running, not a paraphrase, with a copy button. Give it a risograph print-shop look: paper dots, thick ink borders, fluoro pink, teal and yellow.

methodology: Single source of truth: the generated CSS string is injected into a <style> element and also printed, so the spec asserts the printed text equals the live stylesheet — the panel cannot drift from what runs.

Browser as oracle: track counts come from getComputedStyle(gridTemplateColumns) and item bounding boxes, so tests check what Chromium actually laid out (e.g. auto-fit reporting 0px collapsed tracks) rather than re-deriving grid maths in JS.
Hand-computed layout values: span 12 on 10px rows with 8px gaps must be exactly 208px tall; floor((192 + 12) / 72) = 2 tracks after dragging the container to its 220px minimum.
Viewport-independent container tests: the handle's Home/End keys and the breakpoint slider put the frame on known sides of the @container rule on both a 1280px desktop and a Pixel 7.
Input validation: malformed and non-rectangular grid-template-areas are rejected with an inline error and never reach the stylesheet.
Responsive checks at 360–412px with letter-spacing injected, to catch overflow from long CSS values and selects.
risks: Explicit track lists that do not fit narrow phones (fixed px sidebars) squeeze the middle track to 0px — caught while building and fixed by giving the holy grail 1fr 3fr 1fr columns.
The container width readout drifting from the true content box if frame padding or border changes, which would break every container-query assertion.
Pointer capture on the resize handle behaving differently for touch-emulated input.
qa.playwright: Layout is fully deterministic, so there is no need for seeds or fake clocks; the challenge is that the same page has very different widths on the two projects. Instead of branching on isMobile, the tests drive the container to known widths (Home = 220px via the keyboard-accessible slider handle, a mouse drag far past the minimum) and assert values computed from those. Range inputs are set with locator.fill(), which dispatches input events. Screenshot assertions were avoided in favour of computed-style and bounding-box oracles, which fail with a readable diff and are immune to font rendering differences across operating systems.
coverage: auto-fill leaves empty tracks; auto-fit collapses them and widens items
Holy grail areas, keyboard resize into and out of the container query
Pointer drag on the resize handle reflows the grid
Flexbox nowrap, per-item flex-grow, direction column, item reset
Masonry spans and dense flow; printed CSS equals live CSS; copy
grid-template-areas validation errors and area-driven item count

a11y: Every control is a labelled native input, select or aria-pressed button, and the container edge is a focusable role=slider operated with arrow keys, Shift+arrow, Home and End. Items on the bench are real buttons named after their area, and container width, track counts and container-query state are exposed as text.
